newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Oriental Press up on price rise rumour.
newsitem.headline: Oriental Press up on price rise rumour.

text.p: Shares of newspaper publisher Oriental Press Group Ltd touched to hit a year high of HK$4.45 ahead of Wednesday's close fueled by rumours of a newstand price hike which was later denied by the company.
Oriental Press ended at HK$4.375 per share on Wednesday, up HK$0.45 or 11.46 percent from the previous close.

"Anticipation that the company's earnings would be boosted fueled the late buying interest," said a research manager at a local brokerage. Brokers said it was rumoured that newstand price of the paper would raise by HK$1.0 to HK$6.0 per copy.
A company official later denied the price rise rumour.
Among other newspaper stocks, Sing Tao Holdings Ltd also rose HK$0.175 or 5.04 percent to end at HK$3.65.
South China Morning Post rose HK$0.10 or 1.80 percent to HK$5.65 and Hong Kong Daily News rose HK$0.18 or 17.65 percent to HK$1.20, but Ming Pao Enterprise slipped HK$0.025 to HK$2.775.
